headline: The United States, United Kingdom, and seven allied governments warn that Russia's FSB Center 16 is hijacking poorly secured routers to breach critical infrastructure, the same day the EU and UK impose their first joint cyber sanctions on Moscow.

emerging_trends.text: Russia's intelligence services dominated the day, as CISA and eight allied governments warned that FSB Center 16 is quietly hijacking home and small-office routers to reach critical infrastructure, hours after the EU and UK unveiled their first joint cyber sanctions on Moscow.

Attackers are learning to poison the memory and reasoning of autonomous AI assistants, with MemGhost planting persistent false facts through a single email while defenders experiment with context-bombing injections that make hacking agents quit.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agent Memory Poisoning and Prompt-Injection Warfare

emerging_trends.text: Identity and supply-chain weaknesses keep opening the enterprise door, as ShinyHunters-style actors abuse OAuth trust inside SaaS applications and a hack of Lidl's IT provider spills shopper data across three countries.

topics.title: Russian FSB Center 16 Router Campaign
topics.latest_developments: On July 13, 2026, CISA, the FBI, and agencies from eight allied countries issued joint advisory AA26-194a warning that Russia's FSB Center 16 is opportunistically compromising vulnerable, poorly configured routers to infiltrate critical-infrastructure networks and stand up residential proxies.
topics.summary: FSB Center 16 cyber actors exploit internet-facing routers with weak configurations across critical sectors worldwide to gain footholds and proxy their traffic. CISA urges operators to patch firmware, replace default credentials, and disable unused management services.

sources.title: Improve Router Hygiene to Protect Against Russian State-Sponsored Targeting
The US government warns that Russia state hackers are coming after your router
US and allies warn of Russian critical infrastructure attacks

topics.title: AI Agent Memory Poisoning and Prompt-Injection Warfare
topics.latest_developments: The Hacker News detailed MemGhost on July 13, 2026, an attack that plants persistent false memories in a memory-enabled AI assistant through a single email, as Ars Technica reported defenders now firing context-bombing prompt injections that trick hacking agents into shutting down before they cause harm.
topics.summary: MemGhost coaxes an AI assistant into saving a false fact about its user, hides the change, and quietly steers later answers, while security teams build 'yellow team' tools that turn prompt injection into a defense. Enterprises wiring AI agents to inboxes and tools should constrain memory writes and audit agent actions.

sources.title: New MemGhost Attack Plants Persistent False Memories in AI Agents Through One Email
Now, defenders are embracing the prompt injection, too
'Yellow Teams' Are Defining the Future of AI Security

topics.title: Lidl, Centers Laboratory, and Nihon Kotsu Breaches
topics.latest_developments: On July 13, 2026, Lidl notified customers in Germany, Belgium, and the Netherlands that attackers stole personal data through a breached IT service provider, Centers Laboratory confirmed the WorldLeaks extortion group took 720 GB affecting 540,000 people, and Japan's largest taxi operator Nihon Kotsu shut down systems after a cyberattack.
topics.summary: Three organizations across retail, healthcare testing, and transportation disclosed intrusions, two of them exposing large volumes of customer records. Affected customers of Lidl and Centers Laboratory should watch for phishing and identity fraud.

sources.title: Lidl discloses online shop breach after service provider hack
Centers Laboratory Data Breach Affects 540,000 Individuals
Japan's largest taxi operator shuts systems after cyberattack

topics.title: ShinyHunters OAuth Abuse Against SaaS
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Threat Intelligence disclosed on July 13, 2026 that threat actors sharing ShinyHunters tradecraft are chaining voice phishing, supply-chain compromise, and misconfigured guest access to abuse OAuth in SaaS applications and steal enterprise data.
topics.summary: ShinyHunters-linked actors target software-as-a-service platforms through vishing, poisoned supply chains, and loose guest permissions, then abuse OAuth application consent to exfiltrate data. Microsoft advises tightening consent policies, guest access, and application monitoring.

sources.title: Defending SaaS-based applications against ShinyHunters OAuth abuse

topics.title: Russian Coms Spoofing Platform Charges
topics.latest_developments: UK authorities charged five people on July 13, 2026 following a National Crime Agency investigation into Russian Coms, a caller-ID spoofing platform that criminals used to place more than 1.8 million scam calls.
topics.summary: Russian Coms let fraudsters mask their numbers and impersonate banks and officials at scale before UK investigators dismantled it. The case underscores caller-ID spoofing services as a backbone of telephone fraud.

sources.title: UK charges suspects linked to Russian Coms call spoofing platform

topics.title: CISA GitHub Credential Exposure
topics.latest_developments: Krebs on Security reported on July 13, 2026 that CISA published a postmortem after a contractor left dozens of internal agency credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months before KrebsOnSecurity notified the agency.
topics.summary: A CISA contractor exposed sensitive federal cloud credentials in a public repository that sat readable for months, and the agency's slow initial response drew scrutiny. The postmortem urges every security team to scan repositories for secrets and rotate keys immediately after exposure.

sources.title: Lessons Learned from CISA's Recent GitHub Leak

business_politics.title: U.S. Weighs Strike on Iran's Nuclear Site
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump reimposed a full naval blockade, announced a 20% Hormuz transit fee, launched a third straight night of strikes, and said he is weighing an attack on an Iranian nuclear site.
business_politics.summary: President Trump declared the United States the "guardian of the strait" and said Washington will charge ships 20% of their cargo's value for protection in the Strait of Hormuz as U.S. Central Command bombed Iranian targets for a third consecutive night; oil surged nearly 10% past $80 a barrel, Treasury yields rose, and gold fell below $4,000.

sources.title: U.S. Launches New Iran Strikes, as Trump Weighs Attacking Nuclear Site
Trump Says He Is Reimposing the U.S. Blockade of Iran
Oil surges past $80 on Trump threat to impose 20% Hormuz fee

business_politics.title: States Sue to Block Paramount-Warner Merger
business_politics.latest_developments: California and eleven other states filed suit Monday to stop Paramount's roughly $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, alleging the deal is anticompetitive.
business_politics.summary: A coalition of a dozen states led by California sued to block Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, arguing the Hollywood merger would raise consumer prices for TV bundles, harm theaters, and lower film and television quality; the suit could delay the deal and cost the studio tens of millions of dollars.

sources.title: California, Other State AGs Sue to Block Paramount-Warner Megadeal
Democratic states sue to block Paramount's $110bn WBD acquisition

business.title: PJM to Release Capacity Auction Results
business.latest_developments: PJM Interconnection releases its 2028-29 capacity auction prices Tuesday, July 14, a figure advocates expect to push electricity rates higher.
business.summary: PJM Interconnection, the grid operator for Pennsylvania and twelve other states, publishes capacity auction results for the 2028-29 delivery year Tuesday; energy and consumer advocates warn the numbers will drive up electricity rates across the region.

sources.title: PJM Interconnection to release capacity auction results soon. How much will electricity rates go up?

business.title: Pitt, Penn State Win Performance Funding
business.latest_developments: The enacted Pennsylvania budget steers millions in new performance-based money to the University of Pittsburgh and Penn State while holding other colleges' appropriations flat.
business.summary: Pennsylvania's new state budget grants the University of Pittsburgh and Penn State millions in performance-based funds, leaving money for the commonwealth's other colleges stagnant.

sources.title: Pitt, Penn State will get millions in performance-based funds, while money for other colleges stays stagnant in Pa. budget

business.title: Pittsburgh Sues Fire-Truck Makers
business.latest_developments: The city of Pittsburgh filed an antitrust suit Monday against several fire-truck manufacturers, alleging they schemed to monopolize the trucks and parts markets.
business.summary: Pittsburgh sued several fire-apparatus manufacturers and related companies Monday, alleging anticompetitive schemes to consolidate and monopolize the markets for fire trucks and replacement parts.

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh sues fire truck companies, alleges antitrust violations

around_town.title: 23 Townhouses Proposed for Strip District
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh's Planning Commission will hear a proposal Tuesday, July 14, for 23 new townhouses in the Strip District.
around_town.summary: A developer goes before the Pittsburgh Planning Commission on Tuesday to pitch 23 new townhouses in the city's Strip District neighborhood.

sources.title: 23 new townhouses proposed for Strip District

around_town.title: Pittsburgh Restores 'Family Swim' Pool Rule
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh began its "Family Swim" policy Monday, requiring swimmers 15 and under to bring an adult 21 or older to public pools on evenings and weekends.
around_town.summary: For the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, Pittsburgh requires children 15 and under to be accompanied by an adult 21 or older during evening hours and all weekend at city public pools; the city declined to call the "Family Swim" rule a chaperone policy.

sources.title: Pittsburgh's new public pool swim guidelines are not a chaperone policy, mayor says

around_town.title: Code Orange Air Quality, Heat for Tuesday
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania DEP issued a Code Orange ozone alert for Tuesday, July 14, with a Code Red heat advisory as highs reach the mid-90s.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection placed Allegheny, Westmoreland, Armstrong, Fayette, Washington, Beaver, and Butler counties under a Code Orange ozone alert for Tuesday, when sunny skies and highs in the low- to mid-90s will drive ozone buildup; a Code Red heat advisory covers parts of southwestern Pennsylvania.

sources.title: Code Orange Air Quality, 'Code Red' heat advisory issued for parts of Southwestern Pa.

around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette weighed whether Steelers offensive tackle Troy Fautanu, center Zach Frazier, and linebacker Payton Wilson are ready to earn contract extensions heading into 2026.

around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette writers say a revamped offense has the Pirates' clubhouse eager for the second half and confident they will stay in the wild-card race.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette's Noah Hiles and beat coverage described a Pirates clubhouse energized entering the All-Star break, crediting a rebuilt lineup for a power surge and arguing the club will stay in the National League Central and wild-card chase.

around_teams.latest_developments: Pirates ace Paul Skenes said this year's All-Star Game feels "a little bit more of a vacation," though he still plans to make the most of it in Philadelphia.
around_teams.summary: Pirates right-hander Paul Skenes, the club's lone All-Star selection, told the Post-Gazette the Philadelphia All-Star Game feels more like a rest than last year's, and he intends to enjoy the showcase.

sources.title: This All-Star Game is 'a little bit more of a vacation' for Pirates ace Paul Skenes. He still plans to make the most of it
